help_intro: A quick guide to the most important things in the app.
help_workflow_body: Click "Select & Translate" and drag over an area of the screen (Esc or right-click cancels). The translation appears directly over the original text or in the toolbar's text panel - depending on the "Direct overlay translation" setting in the "Interface" tab of Settings. The ⟳ button next to it translates the same area again without selecting it anew - handy for subtitles and text that changes. The overlay has buttons for copying and reading aloud. With "Preserve original font size" ("Interface" tab) the overlay text matches the size of the original text - measured automatically for each newly selected area; if it can't be measured, the size from Settings is used. Drag the toolbar from the empty space between the buttons to move it; the "—" button minimizes it.
help_interface_body: "Aa" opens a window for translating text: type or paste text and translate with the button or Ctrl+Enter; with "Auto-translate" checked, the translation appears a second after you stop typing. The clock shows the translation history of the current session - any entry can be shown again, copied or read aloud; the history is not kept after the app closes. The bottom right of the history shows how many translations were made this session and how many came from the cache (no new request to the service - useful with a paid key). The eye hides/shows the text panel. "Auto refresh" re-translates on a set interval. Already-translated text is served from cache, without a new request to the service. "Restore defaults" in Settings resets all settings (your API key is kept). Under "?" → "Check for updates" the app asks GitHub whether a newer version exists and, if so, opens the download page - only when you ask; it never checks on its own.
help_translation_body: Google, DeepL and Microsoft are online services - if the primary one fails, the app automatically tries Google as a fallback. "On this computer (offline)" translates without internet using free Argos Translate models: in the "Translation" tab of Settings choose the OCR language and target language and press "Download offline languages" (about 70 MB per language pair, once; if there is no direct model, the translation goes through English). Downloaded models are also used automatically when the internet is down. They are kept in the "argos-models" folder next to the program - copy it when you move to a new version so you don't download them again. Offline quality is decent but below the online services. Additional OCR languages can be downloaded with the "Download language" button in the same tab.
help_audio_body: The voice is chosen in the "Audio" tab of Settings (full list of edge-tts voices). Voice playback always requires an internet connection, even when translating offline - the service (edge-tts) is online. Playback speed (0.5x-2x) is set in the same tab.
help_hotkey_body: Two hotkeys: for "Select & Translate" (Ctrl+Alt+T by default) and for "Translate again" (Ctrl+Alt+R). Enable them in the "Hotkey" tab of Settings; when enabled, the combination also shows in the tooltip of the matching button. They work on Windows and on Linux under X11 (not under Wayland).
clear_button_tooltip: Clears the text, the marked area, and the translation cache; stops auto-refresh and closes the overlay, if active
